findings.finding: The new Bedrock InvokeModel client-error alarm the plan stands up gates every landing on main after cross-provider fallback removal, but the plan's Scope and AC specify only thresholds and never require it to wire alarm_actions/ok_actions to aws_sns_topic.alerts. findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly in Approach why a staged/canary rollout is not used (e.g. single review-bot service on the team's own repo, dogfood-by-design blast radius, kill switch + safety-net-first ordering as the substitute for a canary), so the single 100%-traffic flip is a justified choice rather than an unaddressed gap.
evidence: ORDERING AC: 'this cutover removes cross-provider fallback from the gate that reviews EVERY landing on main, so if Bedrock degrades, landings stop until a human runs the kill switch'

No mention of a flag/canary/subset-of-changes rollout anywhere in Approach or Scope — the compose class-slot edit re-points all four passes at once ('filling the slots re-points Pass-1 ... and Pass-2/Pass-4 ... in one act')
Rollback IS present and AC-tested: 'Deleting the three lines above and recreating the container therefore restores the Anthropic path' and the kill-switch end-to-end AC
findings.finding: The cutover is a single 100%-traffic flip of the gate that reviews EVERY landing on `main`, with no staged/canary rollout; the plan supplies a cheap tested rollback (the kill switch) and acknowledges the blast radius, but never states WHY a staged/canary rollout is not used here.
scenarios: Bedrock degrades right after the flip and every landing on main is blocked until a human notices the alarm and runs the kill switch
A reviewer of the plan asks why a canary/staged approach wasn't chosen for a gate this critical and finds no answer
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short paragraph noting that a canary is not applicable to a single-service gate on the team's own repo, that the dogfood premise intends the team to absorb any failure before clients, and that the safety-net-first ordering AC plus the proven token-free kill switch stand in for a staged rollout.

findings.finding: The documented recovery path (kill switch flipping REBAR_LLM_MODEL back to `anthropic:…`) depends on the Anthropic key that this same story retires from the container. Scope says fetch-secrets.sh should 'stop fetching the Anthropic key for this container once the cutover holds', and the final AC requires the container's env to contain NO ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Once that retirement lands, the kill switch flip to the Anthropic path has no credential and becomes a no-op — the very recovery path the ORDERING criterion insists must be proven before it can be needed is disabled by this story's own scope.
findings.location: Approach ('a documented one-line kill switch (`REBAR_LLM_MODEL` back to `anthropic:…`)') vs Scope ('stop fetching the Anthropic key for this container once the cutover holds') and final AC ('contains no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`')
findings.suggested_fix: State that the Anthropic key remains fetchable/available for the kill switch even after cutover (retire only the DEFAULT use, not the credential), OR make the kill switch a documented re-provisioning step (restore the key + flip model) and prove that end-to-end path works.

findings.finding: The subject plan scopes its model-flip entirely to the bot service's single `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` env var (Scope: `infra/compose/` — the bot service's `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` / region environment; and the kill switch reverts `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` back to `anthropic:…`). The prerequisite establishes that one env var cannot express the four/five per-pass model classes the code-review gate requires: opus-family for Pass-1, sonnet-family for Pass-2/Pass-4, and that a single `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` set to opus hard-fails Pass-2 (temperature=0 400) while sonnet-everywhere silently downgrades Pass-1. The subject plan's cutover mechanism (a single `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`) is inconsistent with the per-pass configuration the prerequisite says is required to make this exact cutover work.

The prerequisite establishes model classes (trivial/standard/frontier) as the universal LLM interface and deprecates `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` as a single scalar that cannot express a per-tier mapping; the three verifier paths and the Pass-1 ladder are migrated to resolve classes instead of a single model string. The subject plan's cutover mechanism relies on setting the bot service's `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` (Scope) and reverts via `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` back to `anthropic:…` (kill switch), i.e. it drives the production gate through the single deprecated scalar the prerequisite removes and which cannot express the per-pass class mapping the gate needs.

The Approach names 'the existing tenacity transport retry absorbs transient faults' as the transient-fault/throttling mitigation for the no-fallback Bedrock cutover, but that retrying transport exists ONLY on the Anthropic path, not on the Bedrock path being cut over to.
findings.suggested_fix: State the actual Bedrock transient-fault posture: the cross-region inference profile plus any provider-side retry, NOT the anthropic_model.py tenacity transport (which bedrock_model.py explicitly does not open). If transport-level retry parity is wanted on Bedrock, scope it explicitly.

findings.finding: The happy-path oracle and operator-attested AC assert the LLM-Review (code-review) gate's sidecar provenance names `provider == "bedrock"`, citing S5 [rebar:343b-4fdc-6722-469b]; but S5 delivered provenance only for the plan-review and completion gates — its own record shows the CODE-REVIEW gate verdict never sets provenance and defers it to follow-up ticket e951, which S8 does not cite or depend on.
findings.location: Testing → happy path; AC line 'a real Gerrit change receives an LLM-Review vote ... provenance showing provider == "bedrock"'
findings.suggested_fix: Cite e951 (code-review provenance) as the prerequisite for the provider==bedrock provenance oracle and add the dep edge, or scope the provenance wiring for the code-review gate into S8 itself.

findings.finding: The cutover mechanism is a single REBAR_LLM_MODEL knob, but the code-review gate runs four passes (Pass-1 finder, Pass-2 verify, Pass-4 coach) all off cfg.model with no per-pass split. A single Bedrock model id therefore either regresses Pass-1 finder quality (sonnet), or breaks greedy Pass-2 determinism and silently loses caching (opus) — both wrong, in opposite directions. Additionally the Pass-1 model_ladder uses bare `claude-*` ids that route to direct Anthropic, so a bare re-point produces a split-brain (finder on Anthropic, rest on Bedrock), and `models_at_or_above` escalation returns bare Anthropic ids, hard-failing in a no-key Bedrock container.
findings.location: Approach + Scope ('infra/compose/ — the bot service's REBAR_LLM_MODEL / region environment')
findings.suggested_fix: Make the per-pass model-class configuration a named prerequisite/scope item (the ticket references a config seam / sibling cc33): configure Pass-1 and Pass-2/Pass-4 model ids independently with fully-qualified `bedrock:us.anthropic....` ids, add a test asserting the resolved model per pass under a Bedrock config is the intended class, and assert no bare `claude-*` id survives on any executed path.

findings.finding: The plan says fetch-secrets.sh will 'stop fetching the Anthropic key for this container', but fetch-secrets.sh writes a SINGLE shared .env that is env_file for BOTH the review-bot AND the opcert service, and opcert consumes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for its own gate LLM ops. There is no per-container Anthropic key today, so 'retire the key for this container' is not expressible against the shared file, and removing the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY line would break opcert.
findings.location: Approach ('an Anthropic key in SSM that the cutover otherwise retires') + Scope ('infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh — stop fetching the Anthropic key for this container') + AC 'env output ... contains no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'

findings.finding: The leaf redefines the parent epic's specified CloudWatch alarm. Epic 061c's AC (which names eb6e as its evidence site) requires 'a CloudWatch alarm on the review bot's Bedrock InvokeModel client-error rate — threshold >25% of invocations over a 15-minute window, 2 consecutive periods — publishes to the review bot's existing SNS notification topic. Evidence: the alarm ARN and one forced test notification.' The leaf instead specifies a VOTER_ERROR CloudWatch alarm (rebar's application-level fail-closed signal), proven by inducing a VOTER_ERROR and observing the alarm fire — a different metric subject, with none of the parent's >25%/15-min/2-consecutive-period threshold, no named SNS topic, and different evidence. This is a redefinition of a parent deliverable, not a consistent narrowing.
findings.location: S8 Approach ('a CloudWatch alarm fires on VOTER_ERROR') and Scope ('infra/scripts/observability.sh — the VOTER_ERROR alarm'); AC lines on the VOTER_ERROR alarm; vs epic 061c final AC on the Bedrock InvokeModel client-error-rate alarm
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the VOTER_ERROR fail-closed alarm as the last-resort safety net, but ADD the epic-specified Bedrock InvokeModel client-error-rate alarm (>25%/15-min/2-period → existing SNS topic) as the primary Bedrock-degradation signal, and add ACs capturing the alarm ARN and one forced test SNS notification, matching epic 061c. If the intent is truly to replace the InvokeModel alarm with VOTER_ERROR, take that to the epic first: amend 061c's AC, let its plan-review attestation restale/re-sign, then re-review S8.

findings.finding: The plan's cutover mechanism (a single REBAR_LLM_MODEL env var in infra/compose/) is technically incapable of achieving the stated cutover of the code-review gate as its passes now resolve: code-review.yaml resolves per-pass models through model CLASSES (frontier/standard), read from REBAR_LLM_<CLASS>_MODEL slots, while REBAR_LLM_MODEL is a deprecated bare fallback that collapses all three class defaults onto one model.
findings.location: Approach + Scope ('infra/compose/ — the bot service's REBAR_LLM_MODEL / region environment')
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope/Approach, configure the frontier and standard class slots independently (e.g. REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL=us.anthropic.claude-opus-… + REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_PROVIDER=bedrock, REBAR_LLM_STANDARD_MODEL=us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 + REBAR_LLM_STANDARD_PROVIDER=bedrock), and add an AC asserting the resolved model class per pass under the Bedrock config.

findings.finding: The plan's credential-retirement step and its 'no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY inside the container' AC contradict the shared-.env architecture: fetch-secrets.sh writes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY into one infra/compose/.env that BOTH the review-bot and the opcert services load via `env_file: - .env`, and opcert still needs that key.
findings.location: Scope ('infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh — stop fetching the Anthropic key for this container') + final AC ('env … contains no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY')
findings.suggested_fix: Move ANTHROPIC_API_KEY out of the shared .env into an opcert-only environment source (or a service-scoped env_file), so review-bot's `env` no longer carries it while opcert keeps it.
